analysis:
Changes are small: (1) ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift:82 adds a call to superviseServingAuthorization() in capacityRefreshTick, before writeDaemonState(). (2) ProviderLoop+Serve.swift adds noteCoordinatorConnection(connected:) calls: false after the coordinator client starts (~line 299), event.isConnected on .connected/.disconnected in the connection-control reader (~line 426), and false when the event stream ends (~line 436). The definitions of noteCoordinatorConnection, superviseServingAuthorization and event.isConnected are not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify their behavior.

What I could verify: the new calls sit in the same synchronous actor path as clearConnectionAuthorization() and cancelAppAttestShadow(), and they run before them. They do not alter how serving authorization is cleared, and the existing invalidation on disconnect is unchanged. The periodic supervise call adds a timed re-check of authorization (A-016, T-053, T-057) on the capacity tick. It is a possible strengthening (expiry/revocation), not a weakening. The tick cadence is roughly heartbeat/2 and runs after several awaits, so supervision latency depends on those awaits. This is an availability and timing question, not a demonstrated regression.

The diff shows no new inputs, no change to the encryption path, and no data-exposure change. Nothing here touches the T-041 cache surface.

Open integration questions: (a) whether noteCoordinatorConnection is a pure state recorder or can trigger a side effect such as authorization grant, add-on hold or busy-state changes (TB-012/T-059); (b) whether superviseServingAuthorization fails closed on expiry; (c) whether the initial connected:false before the first .connected could briefly misrepresent state. These need review of the definitions in other files. No concrete finding is supported by the visible evidence.
